There is a small tool that lets the agent say "load the geometry tools for the next few turns". - how is this done? it's a skill that is always loaded into system prompt?

No, it is not a skill and it is not text in the system prompt. It is an ordinary tool, the same kind as "search settings", and the trick is in what the app does after the tool is called.

**How it works**

Every time the app sends a request to the model, it sends a list of tool definitions along with the messages. That list is rebuilt for every request. Today the app always sends the same list. Under this design the app sends the core tools plus whatever toolsets are currently switched on.

The "enable toolset" tool is one of the core tools, so the model always sees it. Its description is a short menu: the toolset names and one line each on what they cover, for example "geometry: place objects, lay out plates, import, delete". That menu is the only thing the model knows about the tools it has not loaded yet.

When the model decides it needs to move an object, it calls the enable tool with "geometry". The app records that, returns a short result such as "geometry enabled: object_place, plate_layout, ...", and then builds the next request with those five definitions included. The model's very next call in the same turn can already use them. They stay switched on for later turns until the model enables something else, or until the app clears them because the project changed.

So the model pays a small fixed cost every turn for the menu tool, roughly a few hundred tokens, and one extra round trip whenever it needs a toolset that is not loaded. In exchange it never carries the full catalog.

**Where this pattern comes from**

It is exactly what GitHub's MCP server does with its "enable toolset" tool, and it is what Claude Code does for you in this session: the Figma and browser tools are deferred, and a search tool pulls their definitions in on demand.

**The alternative**

The app could pick toolsets itself from the project's state: no printer chosen means load setup, nothing sliced means load geometry, sliced means load output. That saves the round trip but the app has to guess what the agent is about to do, and it guesses wrong at phase boundaries. The tool-based version lets the agent say what it needs. Either works, and the guide can be switched to the automatic version if you prefer it.

Short answers: yes, today every tool definition is sent on every model call. Yes, they are cached, but caching only lowers the price, not the context they occupy. And no, the in-app agent should not load 50 to 100 tools per turn. That is what deferred loading is for.

**What happens today**

The in-app agent sends a complete request each time it calls the model, with `store: false`, the instructions, the full conversation, and the whole tools array. That is at [OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp:159](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp:159). There is no "register tools once" step in function calling. The API renders the tool definitions into the prompt in front of the conversation, so in effect they are part of the system prompt, and they are re-sent on every call, including every call inside one turn's tool loop.

**Caching**

OpenAI caches automatically for prompts over about a thousand tokens, on an exact byte match of the leading prompt, and the tools array is part of what gets cached. Cached reads are billed at a steep discount, up to 90 percent, with the newest models charging a bit extra for the first write. So the repeated definitions cost little money once warm. Two limits matter:

- **Any change to the tools array breaks the cache.** That is why a homemade toolset switcher is worse than it looks, and why OpenAI's tool search says it preserves the cache when the model loads a tool.
- **The cache expires after minutes of inactivity.** My recollection is 5 to 10 minutes, so a user who thinks between turns pays full price again. I have not re-verified that number.

**What caching does not fix**

Caching changes the bill, not the model. 50 to 100 definitions at today's measured size are 25 to 50 thousand tokens sitting in the context window on every call, and the model still has to pick among them. Both selection accuracy and the room left for the conversation get worse. That is the cost the budget rule is about.

**So what should the in-app agent load**

The core set, about ten tools, plus anything the model has pulled in through tool search. With `defer_loading: true` the other definitions travel with the request as searchable metadata but do not sit in the model's context until it loads one, and once loaded they stay loaded for the rest of the chat. The per-turn number is then around 10 to 20 regardless of how large the catalog grows.

The one open item is the probe from before: confirming that the pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` accepts `tool_search`. If it does not, the fallback is either a model that does or the homemade switcher, and the homemade switcher costs a cache miss on every switch.

# Handoff: the tools that take a project from a model file to G-code

**Status:** Working handoff, not committed. Written 2026-09-15 for the agent that implements the "journey" tools. The rules live in [the tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md); this document only sequences the work and records the decisions already made. When this document and the guide disagree, the guide wins and this document is wrong.

## Goal

Give the JusPrin agent, in-app and over MCP, every tool it needs to guide a user from opening a 3MF or importing an STL to a G-code file that prints well. That journey, from the guide's candidate catalog, is:

1. Get the model in and learn what it is.
2. Establish which printer, nozzle, plate, and filament will really do the job.
3. Capture intent, and end the back-and-forth by turning unknowns into visible assumptions.
4. Decide geometry: orientation, scale or units, split, repair, quantity, layout.
5. Mark local meaning: protect this hole, keep that face smooth, seam at the back.
6. Choose the technical method: process preset plus setting patches, including supports and adhesion.
7. Slice, read the report, look at the result, and iterate.
8. Export G-code and save the project with its intent, plan, and regions.

Out of scope: sending to a printer, preflight, live printing, camera, calibration, and everything under "Deliberately not tools" in the guide.

## Decisions already made; do not reopen them

- **Load every tool on every turn.** No enable-toolset tool, no tool search, no per-phase loading. The in-app adapter keeps the tools array byte-identical across a chat so OpenAI's prompt cache holds. Record the numbers (below) so the deferral decision can be made later on evidence. If you believe this is wrong for a concrete reason, stop and say so before building an alternative.
- **Tool shape follows the guide's "Tool budget and tool shape" section.** Domain operations, same-shape batches only, reads folded into sections. No tool that dispatches a list of unrelated commands.
- **Names and contracts come from the candidate catalog.** Do not invent new names. If a contract there proves impossible against the real Orca owner, change the guide in the same PR and say why.
- **Every tool follows the guide's implementation sequence and test matrix.** No registry entry backed only by the fake workspace.

## Scope: the 32 tools of the journey

| Toolset | Tools | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `core` | `workspace_inspect`, `object_analyze`, `settings_search`, `settings_get`, `settings_preview_patch`, `settings_apply_patch`, `intent_update`, `plan_set`, `slice_start`, `slice_report` | Five exist and are extended compatibly. |
| `project` | `project_open`, `project_save`, `project_attachment_read`, `history_restore` | `project_attachment_read` returns images; sequence it after the image projection exists. |
| `setup` | `presets_list`, `printer_setup_preview`, `printer_setup`, `printer_list` | |
| `geometry` | `object_place`, `plate_layout`, `object_import`, `object_import_file`, `project_delete_items` | Retires the three fixtures. |
| `reshape` | `object_divide_preview`, `object_divide`, `object_merge`, `object_repair` | |
| `regions` | `region_annotate` | Read back through `object_analyze` `regions`. |
| `check` | `view_render`, `slice_inspect`, `activity_cancel` | `view_render` prepare mode only. |
| `output` | `export_file` | G-code, sliced 3mf, project 3mf, STL, preset bundle. |

## Milestones

Each milestone ends with its eval passing against the real app, the guide's test matrix green for every tool it adds, and the catalog record in the guide updated. Do not start the next milestone's registry entries before the current milestone's real-adapter tests pass.

### M0: machinery every later milestone needs

- **Computation-only policy.** A registry declaration beside `ActionClass` that the coordinator honours; coordinator tests prove no card for `slice_start`, `activity_cancel`, `plan_set`, and a card for `slice_start` with `preempt: true`. Guide section "Computation-only mutations".
- **Output validator keywords.** Add `enum` and `maxLength` to `ToolRegistry::validate_output` with tests before any schema uses them. Guide section "Registry facts worth knowing".
- **JusPrin-owned stores.** Intent, plan, and region annotations in the 3mf auxiliary directory; confirmed printer facts in app data keyed by printer identity with expiry. Extend `ProjectStateDocument` ([ProjectStateDocument.hpp](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.hpp)) rather than adding a second persistence path; it already handles load, migration, and corruption. Add change reasons `Intent`, `Plan`, `Regions`, `PrinterFacts` to `ProjectStateChangeReason` in [ProjectState.hpp](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp) and include them in `kInvalidatingReasons`. Provenance vocabulary per the guide section "JusPrin-owned project state".
- **Output schemas off the MCP wire.** `McpProtocol.cpp` currently emits `outputSchema` for every tool ([McpProtocol.cpp:208](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp)). Stop advertising it; keep `validate_output` on every MCP success. Update the protocol fixtures and the Python bridge tests. Measure the catalog bytes before and after with the offline helper (recipe below) and record both numbers in the PR.
- **Fixture retirement plan.** `duplicate_object`, `import_model`, and `inspect_selection` are removed in the PRs that land `plate_layout`, `object_import`, and the `summary` section's selection ids. Until then they keep their current inputs. Guide section "Input design".

### M1: the core loop on the existing project

Tools: `workspace_inspect` sections `summary`, `intent`, `plan`, `slicing`; `intent_update`; `plan_set`; `slice_start`; `slice_report` sections summary, Orca warnings, conflicts and toolpath outside the bed, material changes.

- `workspace_inspect` gains an optional `sections` input defaulting to `summary`, and `summary` keeps every field the tool returns today so existing callers and fixtures do not break. The `slicing` section is where action-handle state is read; there is no separate activity read.
- `slice_start` follows the guide's "Asynchronous operations" section exactly: start through `Plater`'s reslice path, return a handle, let `ToolActivity` track pending, running, terminal, and invalidated; completion and invalidation publish a change reason. Add a `Slicing` change reason if the existing set cannot express "slice result replaced or invalidated".
- `slice_report` is built from `Print` statistics and the `GCodeProcessor` result already on the plate. Supports, seams, first layer, islands, and intent checks come in M5 and M6 when regions and intent exist.

Eval: from Claude Code through `jusprin-mcp`, "slice the current plate and tell me the print time, filament use, and any warnings"; then change a setting in the GUI and ask again, which must show the stale state and a fresh slice.

### M2: project files and hardware setup

Tools: `project_open`, `project_save`, `history_restore`, `workspace_inspect` sections `project`, `printer`, `history`; `presets_list`, `printer_setup_preview`, `printer_setup`, `printer_list`.

- `project_open` and later `object_import` must never let Orca's dialogs open: inch conversion, oversized model, and load-embedded-settings become inputs. Trace every dialog on the load path the way the settings work traced the normalizer, and add the same "no top-level dialog appears" real-adapter assertion.
- `printer_setup_preview` must be proven read-only by the guide's definition: no dirty preset, no revision advance. If `PresetBundle` cannot evaluate compatibility without committing, say so in the PR and drop the preview rather than fake it.
- The `printer` section reports configured versus observed with provenance and timestamps, and computes `mismatches`. Use the Bambu in-process fake from `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` for the observed side.

Eval: over MCP, open an STL by path with approval, list compatible printers and filaments, set up a printer, plate, and filament, and read back a mismatch when the fake printer reports a different plate.

### M3: geometry facts and placement

Tools: `object_analyze` sections `mesh`, `features`, `orientations`, `fit`, `measure`; `object_place`; `plate_layout`; `object_import`; `object_import_file`; `project_delete_items`; `workspace_inspect` section `objects`.

- `features` needs plane and circle detection callable for a whole object with deterministic ordering. It lives in the Measure module driven by the gizmo; add the smallest product-neutral seam and follow fork stewardship for the upstream lines touched.
- `orientations` reuses `OrientJob`'s evaluation for each candidate; auto-orient inside `object_place` runs as the real job and returns a handle.
- `plate_layout` arrange runs `ArrangeJob` and returns a handle whose terminal result lists objects that did not fit.
- Handles carry the revision they were computed at and fail with `feature_expired` after it moves; test that.

Eval: import an STL that is modelled in inches, fix units, orient it so a named face is down, set quantity two, arrange, and confirm both instances are on the plate and inside the bed.

### M4: settings that make a print good

Tools: the four settings tools extended.

- Expand the write allowlist to the keys the journey needs: the support family (enable, type, style, threshold angle, build-plate-only, interface layers and pattern, top and bottom contact distance), adhesion (brim type and width, skirt), seam position, and the wall, infill, and shell keys not yet allowed. For each key, re-read `update_print_fff_config` and `toggle_print_fff_options` for every place it is read, extend the normalizer hazard table in the guide, and add the real-adapter dialog assertion. This is the largest single piece of work in the handoff; budget for it.
- Add `writable` and `changedOnly` filters to `settings_search`.
- Add the `target` field for per-object overrides through `ModelConfig`, advertised only once tested. Filament and printer scopes stay out of this handoff.

Eval: from a fresh project, enable tree supports on the build plate only with a brim, preview, apply, and prove through the GUI that the tab shows the same values and that no dialog appeared.

### M5: local meaning and reshaping

Tools: `region_annotate`; `object_analyze` section `regions`; `object_divide_preview`, `object_divide`, `object_merge`, `object_repair`; `slice_report` sections supports, seams, first layer, islands.

- `region_annotate` generates modifier volumes, support enforcers and blockers, seam and support paint, and per-object overrides from the semantic kinds listed in the catalog. Regeneration and the `bindingLost` and `artifactsMissing` flags are required, not optional; project Undo can strand either side.
- `object_divide_preview` runs on a clone and must be proven not to dirty the model.
- The supports and seams sections of `slice_report` cross-reference region annotations and detected holes; that is what turns "support enters this hole" into a finding.

Eval: the guide's eval 2. A model with a precision hole and a support-heavy overhang: find the hole, annotate it as protected, re-slice, show supports no longer enter it, and place the seam on a hidden face.

### M6: seeing the result and getting the file out

Tools: `view_render` prepare mode; `slice_inspect`; `activity_cancel`; `export_file`; `project_attachment_read`; `slice_report` intent checks.

- Image results follow the guide's "Image results" section: one registry result, projected as an MCP image block and as an OpenAI image input. Both projections are tested before the first image tool ships. `view_render` uses `GLCanvas3D`'s thumbnail renderer; preview mode is not in this handoff.
- `export_file` shows the destination on the card and surfaces license restrictions from project details at proposal time.
- Intent checks in `slice_report` compare the summary against the intent record, for example time over budget.

Eval: export G-code to an approved path, then reopen the exported sliced 3mf and confirm the report matches.

### M7: grouped approvals

Add the optional `planId` to every mutation and render proposals sharing one as a single card per the guide's "Grouped approvals" section. Do this last, after the tools work with per-tool cards, so the coordinator change is isolated.

### Final eval: the whole journey, twice

1. In-app, with real OpenAI calls: open a one-object STL, state "decorative, front face visible, under five hours, PLA", and reach an exported G-code file with no manual setting edits. The agent must ask only the questions the geometry makes consequential, record the rest as assumptions through `plan_set`, and the exported file must slice without warnings.
2. The same task from Claude Code through `jusprin-mcp`, with every approval taken in the JusPrin panel.

## Cleanup of what exists

- Retire the three fixtures as described in M0.
- `workspace_inspect`, `settings_*`: extended compatibly, never renamed; existing fixtures keep passing unchanged until a field is deliberately added.
- The internal `record_*` tools are untouched.
- Remove any adapter-specific catalog or alias that appears during the work; the registry is the only definition source.
- Update the catalog record in the guide after every milestone so it stays the truth about what exists.

## MCP exposure requirements

- Every journey tool is `InApp | Mcp` except `object_import` (in-app) and `object_import_file` (MCP). Document the reason beside each definition.
- The stdio helper compiles the same registry; its offline `tools/list` must match the live list for the same build. The Python bridge tests in `tests/mcp` cover this.
- Legacy protocol projections in the bridge (`2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-11-25`) must still produce a serialized text result for every new tool; add protocol fixtures per tool.
- MCP annotations (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`) come from the action class; computation-only tools are still `readOnlyHint: false`.
- Path-taking tools (`project_open`, `project_save`, `object_import_file`, `export_file`) read or write the file only after approval, and the card shows the exact path. Test that the file is untouched on rejection.

## Testing requirements

Per tool, the guide's test matrix: registry, decoder, fake workspace ([FakeWorkspace.hpp](../../tests/jusprin_support/FakeWorkspace.hpp)), coordinator, real adapter ([OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp)), OpenAI projection, MCP projection, shell harness. Test files live in `tests/agent`, `tests/mcp`, and `tests/shell`. Build and run with the commands in the guide's "Verification commands" section.

Real OpenAI calls are required, not optional:

- Find the existing live multi-tool regression (start with `grep -rn -i live tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp`) and extend it with the final eval's transcript. It uses the key stored in AppConfig; do not paste a key into source or fixtures.
- For every live request, log the tools array byte size, `usage.input_tokens`, and the cached-token count OpenAI returns, and report them per milestone in the PR. This is the evidence the deferral decision depends on.
- Review each live transcript for wrong-tool selections and for questions the agent asked that the geometry did not justify. Both are eval failures.

Real MCP clients: one end-to-end Claude Code transcript per milestone through `jusprin-mcp`, with approvals taken in the rendered panel, not through a hidden decision hook. Use `--manual-mcp <temporary directory>`, never the user's data directory.

Offline catalog size recipe:

```bash
H=build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/jusprin-mcp; D=$(mktemp -d); printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"measure","version":"0"}}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' | "$H" --discovery "$D/none.json" 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import json,sys; [print(len(json.dumps(t,separators=(",",":"))), t["name"]) for l in sys.stdin for m in [json.loads(l)] if m.get("id")==2 for t in m["result"]["tools"]]'
```

Baseline on 2026-09-15: five tools, 9,723 bytes, about 2,430 tokens, two thirds of it output schemas.

## Fork stewardship

Any line outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` follows [fork-stewardship.md](fork-stewardship.md). Expected seams in this handoff: the Measure feature-detection seam (M3), the load-path dialog choices (M2 and M3), and whatever `Plater` needs for slice completion and invalidation notifications (M1). Keep each additive, record the upstream lines touched, and include rebase evidence. The guide's "Upstream seams the tool system owns" section is updated in the same PR.

## Security gate

The guide's "Proportional security growth" section makes a review a gate before `export_file` (path write) and the computation-only exemption ship. Its minimum outcome is a written answer to each tripped trigger and the per-call approval evidence for every path tool. Do this in M6 before `export_file` merges; it is documentation and tests, not new infrastructure.

## What to report

In each milestone PR: the eval transcript, the test matrix evidence per tool with any "not applicable" layer explained, the measured catalog bytes and per-request token numbers, the upstream seams with rebase evidence, and anything left unverified stated plainly. Do not report a milestone done while any of these is missing.

## Open items that need Kenneth, not a guess

- Whether `project_attachment_read` and `view_render` ship in M6 or wait, since both depend on the image projection work in both adapters.
- Whether the settings allowlist in M4 should go further than the support, adhesion, seam, wall, infill, and shell keys, for example speed keys.
- The `gpt-5.4-mini` tool-search probe is deliberately not part of this handoff.

The guide now says so, and adds one thing: the live regression must record definition bytes, input tokens, and cached tokens per request, so the later decision about tool search is made on numbers.

**What changed in the guide**
